subject: Urgent: inference throughput drop — suspected VPC peering/DNS/proxy path
messages:
From: Lenora Blake <lenora@cobaltretail.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: support@cobaltretail.com
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden inference latency + errors on production (region us-west-2)

Rafael,

We're seeing a severe degradation for our inference calls to model 'redwood-large-v1' across multiple checkout sites — p50 latency up from ~120ms to 1.8s, p95 spiking to 4.3s, and a 30–45% 5xx/error rate on throughput peaks. Traffic patterns haven't changed on our side. This started around 08:50 PT.

Can you confirm if there's anything on Redwood's side (peering changes, routing, DNS)? Our ops team is collecting server-side traces but customers are seeing cart timeouts. This is causing escalations with our retail ops execs.

Lenora
Director of Platform Ops
Cobalt Retail

Attachments: none

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
To: Lenora Blake <lenora@cobaltretail.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 09:28:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden inference latency + errors on production (region us-west-2)

Lenora — thanks for the flag and sorry for the disruption. We're treating this as P1. Initial surface-level checks show elevated SYN retransmits and TCP retransmits between our egress NAT in us-west-2 and the VPC peering path that routes to your edge peering fabric. There are also intermittent DNS timeouts observed in the same window.

What we're doing now:
- Collecting pcap snippets and service logs (attached).
- Spinning up a parallel peering route via our alt-egress (no config change required on your side) to test failover.
- Will run a controlled weighted failover if the alternate path reduces retries.

I'll loop back with a quick exec note once we have a repro and a timing estimate.

Rafael Mendes
Sr. Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pcap-snippet.txt (partial pcap summary), service-logs.zip (500MB stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 10:02:05 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden inference latency + errors on production (region us-west-2)

Quick notes from the runtime team:
- We see request tails with RTOs and packet reordering on the egress path; correlation with increased proxy queue depth at outbound proxy cluster prx-usw-3.
- Metrics: retransmit rate jumped from ~0.2% baseline to 4.7% for the affected subnet 10.24.12.0/22 between 08:48–09:10 PT.

Immediate mitigation plan (15–45m):
1) Move Cobalt traffic to alt-egress path (raf, please coordinate cutover test).
2) Bump proxy worker threads + enable short idle TCP keepalives to reduce socket churn.
3) Put a short TTL override in our resolver for customer-specific hostnames while we validate upstream DNS path.

I've drafted a one-page exec note for Rafael to send to Lenora and her execs; attaching draft (exec-brief-draft.md). If alt-egress shows improvement we'll run a staged rollback and continue diagnostics with cloud provider peering team.

Marissa
Principal SRE — Serving Runtime

Attachment: exec-brief-draft.md

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 11:10:33 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden inference latency + errors on production (region us-west-2)

Status update for execs (draft):
- Impact: Cobalt Retail — degraded inference throughput and elevated 5xx rates between ~08:48–09:30 PT; customer-visible cart timeouts.
- Probable cause: intermittent packet loss and DNS timeouts on primary VPC peering path causing proxy queueing and request retries. Secondary path available; under test.
- Immediate action: traffic moved to alt-egress at 11:00 PT (controlled cut). Observed p50 drop from 1.8s to 150ms in the first 10m, error rate down to ~2.5%.
- Next steps: coordinate with cloud peering team for root-cause (network vendor), run targeted pcap capture on peering hop, confirm DNS resolver health, and propose peering remediation.

I'll attach the short exec bullet list to the customer update. Rafael — recommend sending this update + timeline to Lenora and cc'ing Laura for sales/AM visibility.

Vivek
Head of Incident Response

Related link: https://drive.redwood/incident/RA-2028-03-29

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Lenora Blake <lenora@cobaltretail.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Mar 2028 15:42:10 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden inference latency + errors on production (region us-west-2) — patch applied

Lenora — we completed the controlled move to the alternate egress path and applied the resolver TTL override at 11:00 PT. Metrics through the afternoon show stabilization:
- p50 now ~130ms, p95 ~220ms
- 5xx rate steady at 1.9% during peak windows
- Throughput back to expected levels for your ridership profile

We're still collecting the peering pcap and engaging the cloud peering team for a full RCA (packet loss and occasional asymmetric routing observed). Expected RCA + timeline by EOD tomorrow.

Rafael will follow up with a short exec note for your leadership; Laura will schedule a post-mortem with your platform team next week. Apologies again for the impact — we'll share lessons learned and recommended peering hardening steps.

Neha Kapoor
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: pcap-snippet.txt, service-logs.zip
